en: The Mantra for Vaiśravaṇa, King of the Northern Quarter, Who Protects the Dharma While Accompanying Armies,
translated separately by the Tripiṭaka Master of Daixingshan Monastery, the Great Sage Amoghavajra,
who was specially promoted to the rank of Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial; not included in the canonical scriptures.
Namo ratnatrayāya | Adhakalupatarāya dīrghāya vaiśramaṇāya mahārājāya yakṣādhipataye saptotsada-saśikhāya ||
Rab-ra sa-ha na-ya hi-ma-da-tta hu-vi-pa-ra-sa-ya-me pa-na-ya tha-pauṃ-ni pauṃ-ni ku-śa vai-śra-ma-na-ya ma-hā-ra-dza-ya kha-ba-ga.
Nantarama cihatu mama [Name] dhāraya nasaṃsādhyasana namo bhagavate siddhantu mantrapadāni svāhā.
If a practitioner upholds this mantra:
First, one must paint an image.
Among the pigments, no glue whatsoever may be mixed.
On a white cotton cloth, paint the deity Vaiśravaṇa.
Adorned with armor embellished with the seven treasures,
he holds a halberd in his left hand,
while his right hand rests upon his hip.
Beneath his feet are two yakṣa demons,
both of whom are black in color;
this is the face of Vaiśravaṇa.
He assumes a most terrifying form and glares with evil eyes at all spirits and deities.
That stupa enshrines Śākyamuni Buddha;
he instructs you that if you lead the celestial armies to guard the boundaries and protect the realm, [you shall succeed].
"Who will protect my Dharma?
He then took up and dispatched his third son, Nanda, commanding him to carry [the scripture] and never leave its side, saying:
"Your gaze is poisonous and evil; I fear it may harm sentient beings."
At that time, when the practitioner recites this mantra,
they should do so on auspicious ground.
Do not allow any place to be defiled or foul;
ensure it is perfectly clean and pure, smear the ground with cow dung,
and then coat it with fragrant mud.
One should scatter various kinds of flowers and burn incense as offerings.
The practitioner’s upper and lower garments must both be pure; after using the toilet, one must bathe once.
On the fifteenth night of the waxing moon,
begin by reciting the mantra one hundred thousand times before the image until it is completed.
Thereafter, take fragrant mud once more and smear it upon the altar;
take exquisite, superior flowers and scatter them within the altar;
and provide various kinds of food and drink.
The practitioner takes one hundred and eight grains of incense,
recites the mantra over each one once, and scatters them into the fire.
At that time, Vaiśravaṇa immediately manifests his body.
When the practitioner sees the deity, they should take excellent food and drink to offer to the supernatural power of Vaiśravaṇa.
Whatever the practitioner desires in their heart, the deity will perceive it all.
If the practitioner does not see the deity,
a voice will immediately arise from the midst of space, saying:
"You need only maintain your focus and recite."
"All matters you desire shall be fulfilled according to your wish.
If you see neither the deity nor hear its voice,
there will be only a great wind."
Alternatively, if clouds fill and spread across the altar,
the rite will be accomplished. If none of the aforementioned signs appear, [the rite shall not be performed].
The practitioner shall recite the mantra seven times;
once the one who has entered is bound, the rite is accomplished.
Do not harbor any further doubts.
Furthermore, if a practitioner wishes to gain the love and respect of a king (*rājā*),
they should take a single red bean, recite the mantra once over it,
and cast it into the fire to burn.
Thus, one should recite this one hundred and eight times.
Then the rājā will immediately dispatch someone to summon the person to him at once.
Furthermore, if one wishes to gain the love and respect of high-ranking officials, [one should perform this rite].
Take one grain of white mustard seed;
recite the mantra once and cast it into the fire. After doing this one hundred and eight times, that official will come of his own accord to pay homage with great joy.
Furthermore, there is another method: on the fifteenth day of the waxing moon, construct an altar eight cubits in size before the image;
once it is completed, smear the ground with cow dung.
Having applied a thick coating of fragrant mud,
one should use five colors to paint three concentric courtyards.
Within that altar, in the center, one should draw a great wheel.
Place a four-pronged vajra at each of the four corners in a cross-pattern.
Within the second enclosure,
on the eastern side, paint a fire-jewel from which flames of light issue forth.
On the southern face, draw three prongs;
on the western face, draw a dragon with a lotus flower emerging from each of its mouths;
and on the northern face, draw a large noose.
In the third court, further paint a lion on the eastern side;
on the southern side, paint a dragon king;
and on the western side, paint the peacock-king bird.
On the northern side, paint a rākṣasa standing on the ground with a staff supported in his hand.
At each of the four corners of the altar, place a vase of fragrant water,
containing various fruits and willow branches within.
The mantra-practitioner bathes and puts on fresh, clean garments.
Before the image, he arranges various kinds of food and drink as offerings.
He then recites the mantra and takes a single *harītakī* fruit.
Recite the mantra once for each casting into the fire until it has been burned one hundred and eight times.
From this day forward...
One shall provide one *niṣka* of gold to the mantra-reciter every day so that he never lacks for anything.
Once this object has been obtained, it must be used up entirely;
it must not be kept back.
Furthermore, there is a method: recite the mantra over ghee, honey, and fruit one hundred and eight times and burn them in the fire.
All the devas will be greatly delighted and will protect the mantra-practitioner.
Furthermore, there is another method: if one wishes to travel a long distance,
by reciting this mantra over a pillar made of *śāla* wood while traveling through all difficult places,
one will be entirely free from fear.
Furthermore, if wicked people cause disturbance or harassment,
one should visualize the form of this mantra-deity within the mind and then recite the mantra with focused attention.
If one does not complete even a single round,
that person will be unable to move.
If one desires to do it well:
When the mind is released from the sign of the center, one immediately attains liberation.
Furthermore, if one wishes to cause an enemy not to dwell together with oneself,
one should take one hundred and eight seeds of the *ka-lien-tzu* (kṛtavedana) plant.
If one recites the mantra once and casts it into the fire,
the person will immediately depart from afar.
Furthermore, according to another method, if one recites the mantra over one hundred and eight sesame seeds, [the same result shall follow].
Scatter them into the fire.
Then all people will come to make offerings to the mantra-reciter.
Furthermore, according to another method, if one recites the mantra over white mustard seeds one hundred and eight times and scatters them upon a mountain, [the same result follows].
No evil beasts can harm a person.
Upon seeing such a person, the wild animals immediately prostrate themselves on the ground, not daring to cause injury;
only after the person has passed by do they rise and depart.
Furthermore, there is a method: if one wishes to beg for rain, take one hundred and eight apricot kernels and recite the mantra over them twenty-one times.
Place them in water where dragons dwell, and rain will surely fall.
When wishing to stop the rain, one should take *wutong* seeds and burn them in a fire; the rain will then cease.
Furthermore, there is another method: if a practitioner wishes to beg for food, [he should do so].
First, recite the mantra over the alms bowl one hundred and eight times.
Then, wherever you go,
all food and drink will be spontaneously provided.
When food or drink has been left over, it will spontaneously vanish at that moment.
If one requires food or drink,
one should direct the mind with sincerity toward the bowl and recite the mantra once.
The bowl returns to its original state as before.
Furthermore, if one wishes to see the deity Kung-neng (Kārttikeya),
one should fast for one day and one night.
Before the Buddha, burn *sugandhaka* incense and recite the mantra over one hundred and eight white flowers,
scattering them before the deity.
The deity of that function will immediately manifest their own form,
fulfilling all wishes according to one's needs;
whatever wealth or treasures are sought shall be obtained exactly as desired.
If one wishes to expel all ghosts and spirits,
one should consecrate white mustard seeds and ghee;
for each single seed, recite the mantra once.
If one casts it into fire, it will be obtained immediately.
If there are officials who give rise to unwholesome thoughts toward the Triple Gem, [this shall likewise apply].
Those who harass and disturb the disciples of the Buddha must be subdued in order to cause them to give rise to a mind of loving-kindness.
Recite the mantra over one’s hand thirty-one times and strike [the patient] from a distance; the person will immediately fall ill.
If one wishes for them to recover well, recite it with a compassionate mind once and they will be cured.
Furthermore, there is a method: recite the mantra over earth twenty-one times and scatter it upon one's own body;
then all people who see one will not fail to regard one with reverence and admiration.
If one wishes to cause oneself to possess majestic radiance,
one should recite the mantra over ink and apply it to the forehead;
then all who see one will not fail to regard one with love and reverence.
Recite the mantra over ashes twenty-one times and smear it upon one's body;
all those who see one among the great assembly will perceive marks of merit and virtue,
and the multitude will offer them worship.
If one wishes to travel long distances on the road without being harmed by wicked people or ferocious beasts,
one should perform the mudrā by casting a spell upon the left thumb while running as fast as a galloping horse.
Then, desiring to see matters by looking into a mirror,
one performs a mantra-recitation upon a boy or a girl and asks about good or bad fortune;
that person will immediately speak of it themselves.
If one causes the name of the ghost that afflicts the person to be uttered,
one will immediately know what kind of illness it is.
If the person has been consumed by malevolent sorcery (gudu), [it will likewise be known].
Recite the mantra twenty-one times over the food to be consumed;
the poison therein will be immediately vomited up.
If one suffers from a disease caused by spirits, recite the mantra over five-colored thread.
Recite it once and tie it once, repeating this one hundred and eight times.
Whether tied upon the head, the crown of the head, or the arm,
all illnesses will be cured and eliminated.
If one suffers from a heart disease,
drinking the juice of pomegranate flowers consecrated with mantras will bring immediate healing.
If one wishes to subdue the affliction caused by a fox-demon, [one should do so].
Recite the mantra over five-colored threads,
having the youth join them into a cord;
recite once for each knot, repeating this one hundred and eight times.
Tie it around one's neck.
Furthermore, by reciting the mantra over willow branches and striking the patient with them, the illness is immediately cured.
This applies even to those suffering from ailments in the bones and joints that cause excruciating pain.
If one recites this mantra over a knife as a protection against illness, the disease will be immediately cured.
If one wishes to protect oneself,
one should recite the mantra over white mustard seeds twenty-one times.
The same applies to ashes or water.
By scattering them in the four directions, one establishes a boundary.
If there is illness of the head or the body, one should recite the mantra twenty-one times over clarified butter (*sarpis*) or black sesame oil.
If one smears it upon the body, [the ailment] is immediately healed.
If one suffers from "wind" (vāta) in the ears, reciting the mantra twenty-one times over clarified butter (sarpis) and consuming it will heal it.
If one suffers from eye ailments...
If one suffers from a boil, anoint it with peach oil after reciting the mantra over it;
it will be cured immediately. If one suffers from a swelling, recite the mantra over yellow pomegranate [powder] one hundred and eight times and apply it; it will be cured at once.
Alternatively, white sandalwood may also be used.
If one suffers from a disease of the head,
recite the mantra over twenty-one pieces of turmeric.
If one applies it to the forehead, the ailment will be cured immediately.
If one suffers from the disease of seasonal pestilence (*kāla-vyādhi*),
one should recite the mantra twenty-one times over powdered *śyāmāka* (blue wood) incense.
If one mixes it with water and ingests it, one will be cured immediately.
If one suffers from malignant sores, scabies, or ringworm, one should take the tips of sharp reeds, mix them with oil, and apply them to the affected area; they will be eliminated and healed at once.
If one suffers from malaria,
by reciting the mantra twenty-one times over willow twigs and having them strike the patient, the illness shall be immediately cured.
If one is stung by a scorpion, [the same applies].
Recite the mantra over dried meat and burn it in a fire;
when the heat touches the afflicted area, the ailment is immediately cured.
If one has been bitten by a snake, [the same applies].
Recite the mantra twenty-one times over the *piṣṭa* (ground paste) and apply it;
the affliction will subside and be healed immediately.
If a woman suffers from swelling of the breasts, [the same applies].
If one chews and applies consecrated sesame oil to the affected area, the illness will be cured immediately.
If it is a case of "dengxia" (leukorrhea),
drinking consecrated *dingxiang* water will result in recovery.
If a person is suddenly possessed by a spirit and speaks wildly or incoherently,
one should consecrate water with mantras and have them drink it.
This is also for those suffering from heart disease.
Recite the mantra over yellow earth and smear it [upon the patient].
If one suffers from all manner of malevolent spirits,
recite the mantra over a pomegranate branch one hundred and eight times.
If one uses it to strike a patient, they will immediately recover.
If one wishes to achieve the three matters,
one should construct a mandala before the image.
Having scattered various kinds of named flowers within the altar and finished providing various kinds of food and drink,
take one piece of red copper *phala*.
Take three *liang* of realgar, grind it finely, and mix it with honey-water to form pills;
place them before the image, cover them with lotus leaves,
and shield them with your hand while reciting the mantra without ceasing.
When a sign appears,
if one takes some smoke when it issues forth and applies it to the body,
it immediately becomes an *āñjanī*.
When fire emerges, one takes the flames with the hand and applies them to the face;
all sentient beings who see this person will feel great joy and reverence, perceiving him as possessing great majestic light.
All those who hear the teachings he utters will believe, accept, revere, and follow them in accordance with them.
If there is someone with a feverish heat, one may take [the substance] and smear it upon their body, whereby they shall immediately obtain inexhaustibility.
Furthermore, there is another method: one should recite the mantra over cow bezoar before a stūpa containing relics.
Following the aforementioned medicinal methods, one may apply [the ointment] to the body, whereby all merits and virtues will gather within that person.
Wherever they go, sentient beings will see them as no different from Rāvaṇa.
Furthermore, there is another method: if one knows of a hollow in the mountains that resembles the cave of an asura, [one should proceed].
One should recite the mantra over white mustard seeds mixed with one's own blood;
for every single recitation, strike once at a hole in the mountainside,
until one thousand and eight recitations are completed.
The mountain cave opened of its own accord;
the asura woman’s body blazed like fire as she came forth to welcome the mantra-master, bearing various fragrant flowers.
When a practitioner enters this cave,
their lifespan becomes one great kalpa, and their physical strength is restored to that of an asura;
they are also like a vajra, such that nothing can harm them.
If one wishes to depart, all the asura maidens will follow;
even if one does not return, one will reach the end of the fire without being harmed.
Furthermore, according to the ritual, one should take this image before a stūpa containing relics.
Having finished the supreme offerings by smearing the ground with incense and scattering fragrant flowers within the altar,
take wood from a pear tree to fashion a casket.
Grind the *āñjana* stone into powder and form it into pills using lacquer water from the Qin region.
Place them inside a casket and set it within the altar.
The practitioner, wearing new and clean robes,
shall fast for one day before the image and recite this mantra one thousand and eight times.
There is no need for the exertion of the three phases;
once the mantra has been recited one thousand and eight times, apply it to the eyes.
Then, apply it to the soles of the feet, the centers of the palms, the chest, both shoulders, and the crown of the head.
With a sincere mind, join the palms and contemplate the body as being like space.
When one forms the mental image of oneself as being devoid of bodily characteristics,
the practitioner becomes invisible and can travel a thousand li in a single day.
All ritual activities will be clearly perceived.
Furthermore, if one wishes to subdue non-Buddhists by entering fire,
one should take one's own blood and the blood of fish.
If one recites this mantra twenty-one times with a mind of anger and casts it into the fire, one will enter the flames;
for the duration of a meal, one's body will not be burned.
Furthermore, according to another method, if one wishes to subdue non-Buddhists (tīrthikas),
one should form the mudrā with the hands and recite the mantra one hundred and eight times with a wrathful mind.
All the rites performed by non-Buddhists will be utterly destroyed and none shall succeed.
Furthermore, if one wishes to subdue the armies and bandits of various nations,
one should paint an image of the deity’s body clad in armor of refined purple-gold.
In a clean chamber, burn various renowned incenses, such as *kunkuma* and *turushka*,
and make offerings of flowers of various colors, fragrances, food, and drink. With a sincere mind,
recite the mantra of the Heavenly King one hundred thousand times.
The Heavenly King will lead his celestial armies to come to their aid;
the enemy troops of other kingdoms will naturally retreat and disperse.
If one can recite this without ceasing day and night, [the result will be achieved].
The Heavenly King dispatched his crown prince, Dujian,
to lead a thousand celestial soldiers to guard him, never leaving his side.
Whatever he sought was fulfilled according to his thoughts and in accordance with his wishes.
All shall be accomplished.
Furthermore, if one wishes to subdue an opposing army,
one should observe the fast in a clean room and paint an image of a Heavenly King.
He donned armor of purple-polished pure gold and,
suspended from a twenty-foot pole,
pointed at the enemy fifty paces ahead of the army.
Their adversaries cannot cause them mutual distress.
Interlock the two little fingers as if with a seal;
extend the two ring fingers straight upward and outward.
Interlace the two middle fingers and the two index fingers in opposite directions;
extend the two thumbs outward and upright;
with the palms joined back-to-back, this is the mudrā.
As previously stated, each and every dharma is accomplished by means of this seal.
Now I shall explain the fundamental seal.
With both hands, place the right over the left and interlace the fingers inwardly;
join the tips of the two ring fingers vertically;
and bend the two index fingers like hooks.
When inviting, beckon toward oneself;
when dismissing, wave the hand outward.
When reciting the invocation, form the mudrā at the heart and recite it seven times.
Scatter [the flowers] upon the crown of the head.
Then, taking up the rosary, remain single-mindedly focused on the recitation.
Next, the mudrā of Śrī Devī is explained.

With both hands, join the palms with the hollows facing upward; extend the two index fingers, the two middle fingers, and the two ring fingers so that they are not bent, forming the shape of a lotus flower;
the two thumbs and the two little fingers are held upright and joined together.
When reciting, one should form the mudrā with focused attention;
after reciting the mantra seven times, release the mudrā over the crown of the head.
As stated in the *Caturmahārājika-sūtra*:
If there is anyone who recites this mantra of the Northern Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa and makes offerings of melons,
fruits, and food and drink,
they should select the fifteenth and twenty-first days of each month.
Accompanied by the sounds of single and double-stringed instruments, gongs, and drums,
and while reciting the *sūtra* with a sincere heart, that Heavenly King will immediately manifest his form before one, fulfilling whatever wishes one has in mind.
The *Vimala-viśodhana-dhāraṇī*. Oṃ kuruḍa oṃ. The Eulogy to the Heavenly King *Īśāna* states:

"Benefiting all things, it is indeed the realm of Water; Protecting the national borders, it is our Heavenly King. Worthy generals are entrusted with the charge to consolidate the frontiers; With refined minds they serve their duties, proclaiming and entrusting blessings and auspiciousness. The stellar palace is supreme above, its framework spanning lofty ridges; The sacred image stands solemnly, adorned with myriad jewels. Its majestic spirit vibrates and shines, subduing the wild and remote; Furthermore, through loyalty and integrity, it assists the Sagely Tang. The *Yuanxing lu* (Record of Perfect Conduct) says: [End of quote].
One fascicle of the *Dhāraṇī for the Northern Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa to Protect the Dharma While Accompanying the Army*,
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Amoghavajra as a separate circulation;
the *Record of the Eight Houses* is likewise.
This text was requested to be transcribed by the hand of the Dharma Master Jizō Jishun (慈順僧正).
It is based on the original copy from Tōdaiji (Togawa-san),
which was collated by Aizenin Daiken and others.
I, Kaidō, a monk of Chōkō Valley, have also collated and reviewed the aforementioned manuscript.
On the eighth day of the eighth month of the *Kangen* year, the *Xinyou* (辛酉) cycle, this first proofreading and addition of notes is completed. Recorded by Jishun.
